checks: In dimension N the maximum-simplex normalization places the simplex and body between conv(0,e₁,…,e_N) and [−1,1]^N. The centroid is (1/(N+1),…,1/(N+1)); its coordinate-facet distances are 1/(N+1) and its slant-facet distance is 1/((N+1)√N). Thus the ball of this radius lies in the simplex.
After subtracting the centroid, the coordinate bound (N+2)/(N+1) gives Euclidean outer radius √N(N+2)/(N+1). Dilating by the reciprocal of the inner radius gives N(N+2), including N=1.

An orthogonal map sends the image of the d-dimensional vertical subspace onto the original vertical subspace and preserves both Euclidean balls. The resulting linear part is block triangular, with T invertible by the vertical restriction and A invertible by the quotient. For d=0 the vertical space is zero.

For a Borel E, the sampled fiber over λ=Az+t of K∩F(E) is the image under x↦Tx+Bz+c of the fiber over z of C∩E. The fiber Jacobian is |det T|, so multiplying by |det A| gives the full determinant |det DF|. An exact check with a negative base determinant and a nonzero vertical shear gives the same factor; the shear contributes a translation on each fiber.

Affine images give a bijection of all containing closed halfspaces, not only those of a fixed orientation, so the determinant cancels on normalization. Counting d=0 and the positive-total condition are preserved.
The construction and measure identity match 7cb4b1bb7928127e §§1–2 (1)–(4).

dependencies.comparison: Its maximum-inscribed-simplex normalization applies in ordinary dimension N to any full-dimensional compact convex body. The proof uses just the simplex/cube sandwich after that normalization.

overlap.comparison: Gives the ordinary simplex-to-cube sandwich under unrestricted affine normalization. It supplies the preliminary map but has no vertical-subspace restriction or transformed-lattice/fiber-measure conclusion.

Gives an affine identification of a rank-reduced retained lattice fiber set, preserving its continuous fiber volumes. It does not simultaneously normalize an arbitrary full-dimensional body between Euclidean balls or identify its full affine Jacobian.

readability: The inner ball is centered at the simplex centroid before translation, and the covolume factor is kept separate from the vertical Jacobian.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The simplex normalization can be made vertical-preserving by an orthogonal postcomposition, and the covolume-weighted transformed fiber measure has the exact full affine Jacobian.
